ancestor_decisions: SC1: The evidentiary corpus is exactly seven extracted-text files under papers/text: dung-1995-argumentation.txt (Dung 1995, Artificial Intelligence 77), shapiro-et-al-2011-crdts.txt (Shapiro et al., SSS 2011), lorenz-et-al-2011-social-influence.txt (Lorenz et al., PNAS 108, 2011), du-et-al-2023-multiagent-debate.txt (Du et al. 2023, arXiv 2305.14325), smit-et-al-2023-going-mad.txt (Smit et al. 2023, arXiv 2311.17371), zhang-et-al-2025-mad-question.txt (Zhang et al. 2025, arXiv 2502.08788), choi-et-al-2025-conformity.txt (Choi et al., Findings of ACL 2025).
SC2: Page boundaries in the extracted texts are marked with lines of the form `===== PDF PAGE N =====`, and these markers are the citation anchors required by D12/C3.

SC3: The corpus intentionally contains conflicting empirical conclusions — multi-agent debate gains (Du et al. 2023) versus matched-compute null results and conformity findings (Smit et al. 2023; Zhang et al. 2025; Choi et al. 2025; Lorenz et al. 2011 on social influence undermining crowd wisdom) — and the manifest requires preserving and reconciling these conflicts.

SC4: The envelope's single conversation decision asserts that the seven full extracted texts are present in the solve workspace under papers/text with explicit PDF page markers; the intake envelope itself encloses only the manifest, not the full texts.

SC5: The manifest (material:001) is located at /workspace/seam-harness/research-kb-workspace/CORPUS.md, indicating a benchmark-style workspace named research-kb-workspace under a seam-harness directory.
SC6: The proposed substrate plus the two baselines named in D4 (open conversational forum; no inter-agent communication) naturally supply the three or more conditions required by D14.

context.product_intent: The memo exists to commit the agent system to a single defensible substrate architecture — and to justify that commitment strictly from the supplied corpus — so that recursively decomposing research agents can share, contest, and reuse questions and answers as structured state, capturing the gains reported for multi-agent debate while structurally guarding against the matched-compute null results and conformity failure modes documented in the same corpus.

source_materials.content: Write a 1,400–1,800 word architecture decision memo for a shared knowledge substrate used by recursively decomposing AI research agents. The memo must make a concrete implementable recommendation, not merely survey the literature. Treat questions and answers as first-class many-to-many graph objects: allow multiple competing answers per question, one answer to address multiple questions, question-to-question relations, answer-to-answer provenance or conflict relations, and controlled tags. Compare this design against an open conversational forum and against no inter-agent communication. Specify the data model and invariants, staged visibility and communication protocol, persistence and concurrent-update semantics, contradiction and belief-revision behavior, retrieval/ranking, and the exact role of model versus runtime. Reconcile rather than hide the tension between papers reporting multi-agent debate gains and papers reporting matched-compute null results or conformity. Ground the memo only in the supplied workspace corpus; cite at least five distinct source files with PDF page markers from the extracted text. Clearly distinguish source-supported claims from design inferences. Include a falsifiable evaluation plan comparing at least three conditions, with quality, diversity/correlation, latency, token cost, and recovery-from-wrong-consensus metrics. State important limitations and unresolved questions.

source_materials.content:
# Research corpus manifest

The full extracted texts are available under `papers/text/`. Page boundaries are marked as `===== PDF PAGE N =====`. These source files are the only evidentiary corpus for the benchmark.

- `papers/text/dung-1995-argumentation.txt` — Phan Minh Dung, "On the Acceptability of Arguments and its Fundamental Role in Nonmonotonic Reasoning, Logic Programming and n-Person Games" (Artificial Intelligence 77, 1995). Source: https://cse-robotics.engr.tamu.edu/dshell/cs631/papers/dung95acceptability.pdf
- `papers/text/shapiro-et-al-2011-crdts.txt` — Marc Shapiro, Nuno Preguiça, Carlos Baquero, Marek Zawirski, "Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types" (SSS 2011). Source: https://perso.lip6.fr/Marc.Shapiro/papers/2011/CRDTs_SSS-2011.pdf
- `papers/text/lorenz-et-al-2011-social-influence.txt` — Jan Lorenz et al., "How Social Influence Can Undermine the Wisdom of Crowd Effect" (PNAS 108, 2011). Source: https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1008636108
- `papers/text/du-et-al-2023-multiagent-debate.txt` — Yilun Du et al., "Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate" (2023). Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14325
- `papers/text/smit-et-al-2023-going-mad.txt` — Andries Smit et al., "Should We Be Going MAD? A Look at Multi-Agent Debate Strategies for LLMs" (2023). Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.17371
- `papers/text/zhang-et-al-2025-mad-question.txt` — Hangfan Zhang et al., "If Multi-Agent Debate Is the Answer, What Is the Question?" (2025). Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08788
- `papers/text/choi-et-al-2025-conformity.txt` — Min Choi et al., "An Empirical Study of Group Conformity in Multi-Agent Systems" (Findings of ACL 2025). Source: https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-acl.265/

The corpus intentionally contains conflicting empirical conclusions. The memo must preserve and reconcile those conflicts rather than select papers by desired outcome.
source_materials.label: CORPUS.md
